tb21_profile.skill: Stand up a push-to-deploy chain: create a bare repo reachable over ssh, write a post-receive hook that checks the pushed tree into a webroot, and bring up an HTTP server on a fixed port so the pushed file is retrievable by curl
tb21_profile.domain: git server administration (bare repos, hooks, git-over-ssh) plus a web server bound to port 8080 serving a document root
tb21_profile.task_form: configure-a-service: several cooperating pieces wired together, verified end to end by a client round trip

verifier_notes: CORRECTION PASS (fix-team 03, verifier_strength.json now authoritative). tw_220186 was held out of final_top10 only because the packet graded it FREE; it is `ok` (3 tests, 2 substantive) and is now promoted to rank 9. It went in at the expense of tw_28581, which I re-read in full and which the earlier pass described wrongly: it is not a shell task that clones an app into /var/www/html, it is 'write /app/launch_instance.py using the shade library to launch an OpenStack instance', and the git-clone-into-/var/www/html text only appears as a literal inside the userdata string. Its five tests are pure substring greps over the script source - nothing is ever executed - so its `strong` grade is the heuristic being fooled by regexes over source text, and its apparent similarity to this TB2.1 task is exactly the lexical false positive the spec warns about. tw_306284 is also rehabilitated (FREE -> strong) but I did not promote it: every one of its five tests greps /app/setup.sh for patterns like `systemctl.*enable.*httpd`, the script is never run, no server is ever shown to answer, and the task is graded easy - it teaches writing plausible-looking sysadmin text, not wiring a service up end to end. Retained from the original pass: the packet's inline `verifier` field and work/verifier_strength.json disagree on 2,677 of 9,968 shown candidates pool-wide. system-administration_20260601_053159_005 is a very close git-server match but grades `behavioral`, so it lost its slot to strongly-graded siblings.

notes: Retrieval did well here for once - TMax and CalibForge both surfaced genuine push-to-deploy tasks in their shortlists. CalibForge is the standout: it has an entire system-administration git-hosting family (nginx + git-http-backend + cgit + git-daemon + ssh push), almost all `strong`, and system-administration_20260415_094424_002 is a near-duplicate of this TB2.1 task. TMax's hook-driven deployment cluster is the other strong pool and I took four of the final ten from it. Terminal-Lego turns out to be surprisingly usable: it has dozens of bare-repository-as-remote tasks (mostly `strong`), plus task_01110 (Python HTTP server on port 8080 over www/) and task_00129 (Apache document root) which cover the webserver half; its weakness is that each task is only one narrow slice. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is all `absent` and its git content is client-side (submodules, plumbing commits, push to a bare repo) with only one hook task, rts_task_c2da491633856d902bbafc85. SWE-Rebench's dulwich cluster is a better answer than its shortlist gave: rank 1 there is index-checkout, which is literally what a post-receive hook does. SWE-Smith contributes only web-server-library bugs and scores accordingly.
